project.name: elfutils
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout inside `gt-arvo_45636-workspace` is on commit `9a36370010df049b1d301a5531246ec7a693b95b`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The exact vulnerable file `libelf/elf_begin.c` in that staged tree still lacks the `if (!isdigit (string[0])) return NULL;` guard added by `patch.diff`.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `unknown-crash` because the read walks off a memory-mapped archive field into a wild address range rather than a tracked heap or stack object.

bug_description.original: Project: elfutils. Fuzz Target: fuzz-libdwfl. Crash State: read_long_names __libelf_next_arhdr_wrlock dup_elf. Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 8192-byte file `poc` (sha256 `14418f297ebb70db44a35c59c8a8b2e17ecc13c10091360cfca0c3103340182e`), which `file` identifies as a current `ar` archive and whose first bytes are `!<arch>\n/5603...`. `dwfl_report_offline()` admits it as an archive, `process_archive()` asks libelf for the first member, and `__libelf_next_arhdr_wrlock()` interprets the first member name `/5...` as a long-name reference, so libelf calls `read_long_names()` to scan archive headers for the `//` table. On the crashing scan iteration, `read_long_names()` leaves `string = hdr->ar_size` pointing at the mapped 10-byte `ar_size` field because that field's last byte is a space, but the vulnerable source never enforces the fix's `isdigit(string[0])` precondition before calling `atol`. `len = atol(string)` therefore treats a malformed fixed-width archive field as an open-ended C string and walks beyond the 10-byte field. AddressSanitizer records the resulting `unknown-crash` as a `READ of size 985` in `__interceptor_atol`, with the top project frame at `read_long_names` line 766.

tainted_value_origin.description: The concrete attacker-controlled value that reaches the sink is `string`: on the crashing `read_long_names()` iteration it aliases a candidate header's fixed-width `ar_size` bytes inside the mmapped archive instead of a bounded copy, so `atol` later consumes raw mapped bytes as a C string.
tainted_value_origin.note: Stage 01's saved artifacts do not identify which earlier scan iterations preceded the crash, so this location denotes the final candidate-header parse shared by the crashing path.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that materializes an attacker-controlled archive-member header from the mmapped witness. The loaded `ar_name` field is immediately used to decide whether the member name is ordinary text or a long-name-table reference.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 8192-byte `ar` witness at `gt_results/arvo_45636/poc` (sha256 `14418f297ebb70db44a35c59c8a8b2e17ecc13c10091360cfca0c3103340182e`). After `determine_kind()` admits the archive magic `!<arch>\n`, libelf mmaps the file and line 861 reads the first 60-byte member header at offset `SARMAG`; the header name begins with bytes `2f 35 36 30 33` (`/5603`), which later satisfies the long-name-reference branch.

root_cause.description: Missing digit-start validation before `atol`. `read_long_names()` only decides whether to copy `ar_size` based on the field's last byte, so it can still pass a malformed fixed-width `ar_size` field to `atol` even when the field does not satisfy the decimal-digit precondition added by the fix.
root_cause.note: The fix inserts `if (!isdigit (string[0])) return NULL;` immediately before this call.

sink.description: Closest project-code sink for the saved AddressSanitizer failure. This call site passes `string` into `atol`, and the runtime overread is then reported from `__interceptor_atol`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 985` in `__interceptor_atol` with `read_long_names /src/elfutils/libelf/elf_begin.c:766:13` as the top project frame.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run on the exact staged 8192-byte `poc` reproduces AddressSanitizer `unknown-crash` in `read_long_names` while `fuzz-libdwfl` feeds the file into `dwfl_report_offline()`.

format.name: AR archive
format.contract: Exact-match witness only: the staged 8192-byte `current ar archive` file `poc` (sha256 `14418f297ebb70db44a35c59c8a8b2e17ecc13c10091360cfca0c3103340182e`). It must preserve archive magic `!<arch>\n`, a first member header whose name begins `/5` so `__libelf_next_arhdr_wrlock()` treats it as a long-name reference, and the malformed long-name-table scan state that reaches `read_long_names()`'s `len = atol(string)` without the later `isdigit(string[0])` guard. Stage 02 does not claim a broader malformed-archive family beyond this witnessed file and that source-level missing obligation.

coarse_trace.summary: After libelf admits the staged file as an archive, libdwfl routes it through `process_archive()` instead of the ELF-only `process_elf()` path.
Archive-member iteration calls `elf_begin(fd, ELF_C_READ_MMAP_PRIVATE, archive)` to duplicate the first member descriptor from the attacker-controlled archive.
The first member header name begins `/5`, so libelf interprets it as a long-name reference and calls `read_long_names()` to scan archive headers for the `//` long-name table.

On the crashing scan iteration, libelf parses a candidate header's fixed-width `ar_size` field with `atol` without first checking that the field starts with a digit. The resulting `atol` walk escapes the 10-byte field and AddressSanitizer reports the wild read.

fine_trace.note: Source. While duplicating the first archive member, libelf reinterprets the mmapped witness bytes at the current archive offset as a `struct ar_hdr`. In the staged PoC this header name starts `/5603`, which is the dispatch key for the long-name-reference path.

Because the current member name has `'/'` in byte 0 and `'5'` in byte 1, libelf treats the member as a long-name reference. Since the long-name table has not been loaded yet, this branch invokes `read_long_names()` to scan attacker-controlled archive headers for the `//` table.

On the final `read_long_names()` scan iteration that reaches the crash, libelf reinterprets the candidate archive header at the current `offset` directly from the mmapped file. Earlier scan iterations are ordinary loop plumbing and are omitted; this step names the candidate header that feeds the crashing `atol` call.

This block decides whether `atol` will see a bounded copy or raw mapped archive bytes. The observed 985-byte read in `__interceptor_atol` implies the crashing iteration kept `string` as the mapped `hdr->ar_size` pointer rather than the explicit `buf` copy, because only the direct-pointer path lacks a terminator.

The vulnerable source calls `atol` even though it has not enforced the fix's `isdigit(string[0])` precondition on this fixed-width archive field. With `string` still pointing at raw mapped bytes, `atol` walks beyond the 10-byte `ar_size` span; AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 985` in `__interceptor_atol` with this statement as the top project frame.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the exact missing `if (!isdigit (string[0])) return NULL;` guard immediately before `len = atol (string);`, preventing `read_long_names()` from feeding malformed fixed-width `ar_size` fields into `atol`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness begins with archive magic `!<arch>\n`, so `determine_kind()` returns `ELF_K_AR`. `process_file()` then routes the input into `process_archive()` and archive-member parsing instead of rejecting it as a non-ELF object.
